Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
618 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 216 AM EST Thursday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 216 AM EST Thursday...

1. Showers will be widespread through early afternoon, and then
more scattered towards evening when a rumble of thunder is
possible.

2. Some additional showers are expected over the weekend as 
temperatures gradually return closer to normal. 

3. Somewhat unsettled weather is expected for much of next 
week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 216 AM EST Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Anomalous moisture, with PWAT more than 200% of normal, 
and likely near record for the date per Albany, NY sounding 
climatology, will be present today as a slug of showers slides 
northeastward across the region this morning. Despite this
impressive moisture and very warm air in place, rainfall looks 
meager as forcing for ascent is weak given a lagging shortwave 
trough and lack of frontogenesis. That said, low to mid-level 
lapse rates look to be sufficient for some instability and brief
downpours in some of the showers, especially towards midday 
which helps southern and eastern portions of Vermont have better
odds of these heavier showers. Think these will be brief such 
that total rainfall amounts in a given hour will at most be 
about 0.25" and mainly up to 0.1". 

After this swath of showers and deep moisture exits to our 
east, partial clearing will support some warm season type of 
heating and skinny CAPE profiles that bring us a non-zero chance
of thunderstorms towards evening. HRRR/RRFS guidance has been 
consistent in showing a broken line of showers forming in 
northern New York and gradually translating eastward with 
increasing MUCAPE, progged to reach about 200-300 J/kg. Chances 
of thunder in the calibrated REFS data is surprisingly high in 
far northern Vermont (around 30-40%) based on this CAPE. 
Greatest chances of a rumble of thunder appears to be during the
mid- afternoon near Route 11 in northern New York and then 
during the evening in eastern Franklin County in Vermont. Most
of the remainder of the night, aside from this possible cluster
of showers exiting to the east, will be dry and mild. Much of
Friday continues to look dry and unseasonably warm despite being
a bit cooler than today.

KEY MESSAGE 2: We continue to expect an unsettled weather 
pattern for the weekend, as a closed upper level low ambles 
eastward from the eastern Great Lakes Friday night into the Gulf
of Maine by Sunday afternoon. Its slow movement will provide a 
prolonged period of shower chances across the region, but it 
remains hard to pinpoint where/when rain showers will pivot 
across a particular location. Generally Saturday afternoon 
through Saturday night looks like the timeframe where showers 
should be most abundant over northern New York and Vermont given
the proximity of this system, and the track will favor southern
portions of our region with regards to rainfall amounts. 

While a big soaking rain is not expected, a wetting rainfall of
0.25" through the weekend has increased a bit to a 50-65% 
chance, while rainfall in excess of 1" is now about 10-15%, 
except 20-25% in portions of western Vermont in the Winooski and
Mad River Valleys and the western Adirondack region. With the 
expected low pressure track, we also should see some increasing 
northerly flow towards late Saturday but there isn't much cold 
air to advect in. Most guidance shows 850 millibar temperatures 
too warm for snow, but at this point have indicated marginally 
cold conditions for some snow to mix in with the rain at our 
higher elevations in New York before precipitation ends given 
uncertainty in the upper level low track/strength.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Although there remains differences in model solutions, 
overall we look to remain under cyclonic flow for much of next week. 
The GFS does try to build ridging in briefly for Mon/Mon night, but 
this is not supported by either the ECMWF or CMC deterministic 
solutions, which have multiple shortwaves rotating around upper low 
pressure centered to our north. Timing of these differ as well, so 
while there will likely be some dry days, have stayed with WPC/NBM 
PoPs which give chances for showers through much of the week, 
especially over the higher terrain. Highs in the 40s/50s mean 
showers should be rain during the day, but overnight lows near or 
below freezing could allow rain to mix with/change over to snow 
overnight, especially in the mountains.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...VFR conditions early in the period will 
give way to MVFR as rain showers spread from west to east. The 
bulk of the precipitation will occur through roughly 18z Thu, 
with scattered showers to persist through 00z Fri. Visibility 
generally 5-6SM in any rain, with ceilings lowering to 1500-2500
ft during the daylight hours. There could be some improvement 
after 00z, but generally anticipate MVFR conditions to prevail
much of the night. South winds will remain gusty at KBTV 
through much of the period. Elsewhere, S/SE winds will remain 
less than 8 kt through early this morning, then becoming gusty 
to 18 kt after 14z. Gusts will abate after sunset with winds 
trending more toward S/SW. A 30+ kt LLJ will bring periods of 
LLWS through 18z, particularly at KRUT/KSLK/KMPV.


Outlook...

Friday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Chance SHSN.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect for today on the broad lake. 
South winds currently are likely 20 to 30 knots, expected to
peak early this morning prior to rain arriving. After a lull
during the rain, winds will likely pick up again for a few
hours, likely after 2 PM and before 7 PM, when winds could 
occasionally be near 25 knots. Waves will tend to be 2 to 4 
feet during the period.

&&

.CLIMATE...
As of 216 AM EST Thursday...

Following records set on Wednesday, a high minimum temperature
is possible at BTV today. 

Forecast: 58 
Record: 60 in 2022

VT...None.
NY...None.
